standard_prerequisites.name: Integrality criterion for finite ring homomorphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts integrality of the generators into finiteness of the relative Frobenius.

core_obligations: Translate the statement into the algebra fact: for a finite type homomorphism A -> B of characteristic p with B' = B tensor over (A, F_A) with A, the relative Frobenius F_{B/A} : B' -> B must be finite (proof lines 7161-7165).
Choose generators x_1, ..., x_n of B over A and observe that x_i^p = F_{B/A}(x_i tensor 1), so each x_i is integral over B' (proof lines 7166-7167).
Conclude finiteness of F_{B/A} from the integrality criterion for finite ring maps (proof lines 7168-7169).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the sheaf statement to the affine algebra statement.
Realize the generators as integral elements over the base change.
Apply the integrality criterion for finiteness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a scheme X over S in characteristic p with X -> S locally of finite type, the relative Frobenius F_{X/S} is finite. The proof translates to algebra: for a finite type homomorphism A -> B of characteristic p rings with B' = B tensor over (A, F_A) with A and F_{B/A} : B' -> B given by b tensor a maps to b^p a, the assertion is that F_{B/A} is finite (proof lines 7161-7165). Choosing generators x_1, ..., x_n of B over A, one has x_i^p = F_{B/A}(x_i tensor 1), so each generator is integral over B', and the integrality criterion for finite ring maps gives finiteness (proof lines 7166-7169). H2: the identification of the generators as integral elements over the Frobenius base change is the substance.
